JUDGMENT
This suit is filed by the plaintiff against the defendants for permanent injunction in respect of Site No. 140.

Formed in Survey No. 57 to 82 of Dommalur Village Civil Area, Kasba Hobli, O.S. No.
2814/2015 Bengaluru North Taluk, in the layout plan sanctioned by BDA, which is known as Amarjyothi House Building Cooperative Society. Measuring east to west towards northern side, 118 feet, Towards southern side 135 feet.
North to south towards eastern side 60 feet.
North to south towards western side 60 feet.
Totally 843.33 square yards.
This property hereinafter referred as suit property.

2. According to the case of the plaintiff, he is in physical possession and enjoyment of the suit property as absolute owner, he and Pushpa Deshapande have purchased the suit schedule property by way of registered sale date dated 16.06.1993.
Plaintiff stated that Pushpa Deshpande has executed relinquishment deed dated 06.06.1996 in favour of the plaintiff.
Therefore, the plaintiff became sole owner of the suit property.
The khata of the suit schedule property transferred in his name and he was paying property tax to BBMP.
3. On 25.02.2015, the defendants came along with goonda elements with JCB and pokers illegally demolished the structures standing in the suit property.
Despite protests made by the plaintiff, the defendants used criminal force and demolished O.S. No. 2814/2015 the structure.
The plaintiff immediately rushed to old airport police station and gave complaint against the defendants.
The jurisdictional police have failed to register the case.
They made plaintiff to run from pillar to post.
Therefore, at last, the plaintiff thought it proper to approach the Civil Court.
The plaintiff stated that the defendants has filed OS No. 8488/2011 against other site owners.

In the said suit, Interlocutory application filed by the defendants came to be dismissed on merits vide Order dated 09.03.2012 Neil Deshpande vs Diwakar J Reddy on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52313590/
2 before 39th Additional City Civil and Sessions Court, Bangalore.

sentences.text: 4. The plaintiff stated that the family members of the defendants including the defendants have no prima facie case.

The defendants have leveled the entire sites formed in the said layout and they have dumped huge building materials covering the entire land by putting compound inclusive of the suit property and on 21.03.2015 they came near the suit schedule property and tried to fence the suit property.

The act of the defendants was resisted with great difficulty and therefore the plaintiff approached the court seeking permanent injunction against the defendants O.S. No. 2814/2015 restraining them from interfering in his possession and enjoyment of the suit property.

Therefore,
he prays to decree suit.
5. The suit summons issued to the defendants.
The defendant no. 2 placed exparte.
Other defendants are appeared through their counsels.
6. The defendants no. 1, 3 to 5 have filed the written statement.
They denied the plaint allegations in toto.

The defendants contended that suit for bare injunction filed by the plaintiff is not maintainable when the defendants have categorically denied the title of plaintiff and asserting adverse title over the suit property.

The defendants stated that the Land Survey No. 67/1 situated at Dommaluru Village, Kasba Hobli Bengaluru North Taluk was measuring 1 acre 6 guntas which is stated as A schedule property in the written statement.
This property belongs to D.P.Veerappa Reddy.
He had a wife by name Chikkamma.

Out of the wedlock, they had got three sons by name C.Jayarama Reddy,
S.Sampangirama Reddy and Gurumurthy Reddy.
During the lifetime of Veerappa Reddy, the family members have entered into partition, which is registered on 14.12.1972.
As per the registered partition deed, the A schedule property in the partition deed was allotted to she Jairam Reddy.
The revenue records were transferred in the name of she Jairam Reddy.
He was in possession and enjoyment of the same.
During the lifetime of C.Jayaramareddy, A schedule property was acquired for formation of Amarjyothi House Building Co-operative Society.
The Amarjyothi House Building Co-operative Society was indulged in land acquisition in illegal manner.
The cases were filed by various landowners against the housing society including Amarajyothi House building Co-operative Society before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
The Government of Karnataka also initiated proceedings against the societies including Amarjyothi House Building Co-operative Society.

Hon'ble High Court has constituted a committee known as G.V.K. Rao Committee and as per the findings of the said committee, it was clearly held that the housing societies including Amarajyothi was indulged in bogus and illegal activities.
They have procured the lands through middlemen by paying the authorities the extraneous consideration for the benefit of non-members and carrying on real estate business.
Therefore Hon'ble High Court found several illegality in O.S. No. 2814/2015 the acquisition proceedings and quashed all the land acquisition proceedings.
8. The order was challenged by the House Building Cooperative Societies before Hon'ble Supreme Court.

The Amarajyothi House Building Cooperative Society filed SLP No. 13114 and 13339 of 1991 Neil Deshpande vs Diwakar J Reddy on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52313590/
3 against the State of Karnataka and others.

sentences.text: The Amarjyothi House Building Co-operative Society challenged the order of Hon'ble High Court setting aside preliminary and final notification of land acquisition made in favour of this society.

After adjudication Hon'ble Supreme Court upheld the order of Hon'ble High Court and set aside all the land acquisition proceedings and Hon'ble Supreme Court directed the land owners to re-deposit the compensation amount they have received and Hon'ble Supreme Court directed the House Building Cooperative Society and State Government to restore the possession to the land owners.

The Government of Karnataka, in compliance with the order of Hon'ble Supreme Court, by way of Official Memorandum dated 12.12.2009, ordered that the possession of A schedule property acquired earlier for Amarjyothi House Building Co-operative Society was cancelled and O.S. No. 2814/2015 possession of A schedule property was restored to the defendants.
Thus, the illegal acquisition of Survey No. 67 / 1 was quashed and land was returned to the landowners i.e. The defendants.

9. The defendants contended that they approached the Deputy Commissioner for change of khata,
but the Deputy Commissioner has issued endorsement stating that RTC's in respect of the said village is not continued from 1995 in view of the fact that the lands comes under the jurisdiction of BBMP.
The Deputy Commissioner has directed landowners to approach BMP for transfer of khatas.
Accordingly, the defendants approached Additional Commissioner East Zone BMP.
The khata was effected in the name of defendant in respect of A schedule property.
They have constructed compound wall including the sets in the B schedule property.
Therefore, B schedule property and A schedule property are in actual possession and enjoyment of the defendants.
The defendants denied the fact that the plaintiffs are in possession and enjoyment of the suit property.
Therefore the defendants sought to dismiss the suit.
Based on the pleadings my predecessor in office has framed the following issues.

ISSUES.
1 Whether the plaintiff proves that he is in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property?
2. Whether the plaintiff proves the alleged interference by the defendants in the suit schedule property as contended in the plaint?
3. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief of permanent injunction as prayed in the plaint?
4. What Order or decree?
11. The plaintiff executed special power of attorney in favour of his father.
His father was examined as PW1.
Ex. P1 to Ex. P12 were marked on behalf of the plaintiff.
The plaintiff closed his side.
The defendant no. 1, 3 and 4 have executed power of attorney in favour of DW-1.
He was examined as DW1.
Ex. D1 to Ex. D27 were marked on behalf of the defendants.
They closed their side.

sentences.text: At the fag end the trial, the advocate for plaintiff filed memo stating that he is going to retire from the case.
The memo O.S. No. 2814/2015 was filed on 11.10.2025.

In the memo of retirement,
the advocate for plaintiff intimated the next date of hearing as 11.09.2025 and also mentioned the stage as argument.
On the date fixed for hearing i.e. On 11.09.2025, the plaintiff or the power of attorney holder of the plaintiff remained absent.
I have permitted the advocate for plaintiff to retire.
13. On the same day, I heard the arguments of advocate for defendant no. 1, 3 and 4.
Advocate for defendant no. 5 adopted the arguments of advocate for defendant no. 1, 3 and 4.
The advocate for defendant no. 1, 3 and 4 filed list with one decision.
Subsequently on 17.11.2025, C.G. Gopalaswami advocate filed vakalath for plaintiff with no objection from earlier advocate and sought time to advance the argument.
On the next date of hearing, he remained absent.
There was no representation on behalf of the plaintiff.
The advocate representing the plaintiff prays time for arguments.
Since it was old matter, prayer was rejected.
However, liberty is reserved for the plaintiff to file written arguments.
Since from then the plaintiffs not filed the written argument.
Therefore argument of the plaintiff taken as heard.
My answer to the above issues are as follows.

Issue Nos:- 1 to 3 in negative.
Issue No. 4 :- as per final order for the following REASONS.
15. Issue Nos. 1 to 3.:-Since all these issues are interlinked with each other based on common facts

,
finding
on one issue has great bearing on another issue.
Therefore, all the issues are taken together for discussion.
Before averting to the factual aspect, let me remember the admitted facts in this case.
It is undisputed fact that previously the Land Survey No. 57 to 82 of Dommaluru Village was acquired for formation of Amarajyothi House Building Co-operative Society.
Several sites were formed in these survey numbers.
Among them, the Site No. 140 is one of the same.

It is also undisputed fact that subsequently the land acquisition proceedings initiated by the State Government in the Bangalore City for different house building co-operative society was quashed on a representation and the repetition filed by the landowners.
The respective house building societies have moved to Hon'ble Supreme Court by filing SLP.
In SLP No. 11482 of 1990-91, filed on behalf of HMT House Building Co-operative O.S. No. 2814/2015 Society against the Government of Karnataka and the landowners.

entities.text: HMT House Building Co-operative O.S. No. 2814/2015 Society
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court considered the several House Building Co-operative Society and considered the committee constituted by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka under the the stewardship of G.V.K.Rao came to the conclusion that the house building cooperative society is illegally involved in real estate business.
They are purchasing the property through middlemen.
Therefore Hon'ble Supreme Court has quashed all the land acquisitions made in favour of house building co- operative society is covered in SLP No. 11482 of 1990.
In the said judgment itself, the Amarjyothi House Building Co-operative Society is also included.

sentences.text: The defendants in their written statement took specific contention that after dismissal of the SLP filed by Amarjyothi Hospital Cooperative Society by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, they moved an application for restoration of the Survey No. 67 / 1 to them.
Accordingly, By virtue of Official Memorandum dated 12.12.2009, the Special Land Acquisition Officer ordered the possession of residual property.
The Plaintiffs produced Ex. P1 to 12.
Those are the sale deeds, encumbrance certificates, O.S. No. 2814/2015 khata certificates, khata extracts, tax paid receipts, possession certificate etc, in respect of the suit property.
No doubt the Site No. 140 was issued in favour of the son of PW1.

However, by virtue of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the SLP referred above, entire land acquisition proceedings initiated in favour of Amarjyoti House Building Co-operative Society was quashed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
Therefore, these documents are not helpful to claim that the plaintiff has Is in physical possession and enjoyment of the suit property on the date of filing of the suit.
17. Apart from it, PW1 in the cross examination stated that he had no documents to show that there was a construction in the suit property put up by his son.
He stated that he has obtained plan from BBMP to put up the construction over the suit property.
This is the vital and important document to prove the possession of plaintiff over the suit property.
Non production of vital and important document compels me to draw adverse inference that there was no such sanction plan approved by the BBMP to put up construction in the suit property.
The PW1 was confronted with two photos which are marked as Ex. D1 and D2.
He stated that Inside the compound wall, the defendants have constructed a shed and the compound wall is also constructed by the defendants.
He expressed his ignorance regarding the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amarjyothi House Building Co-operative Society and also Change of khata in the name of defendants.
18. On the other hand, the defendants have produced khata extract, tax paid receipt.

In respect of the A schedule property, A schedule property was transferred in the name of Shyamala Shekaran,
Divakara J Reddy, Shalini J Reddy, Venkatesh Reddy, Deepak J Reddy.
Their property is totally measuring 8712 square feet.
19. They have taken electricity connection which can be evidenced on perusal of Ex. D11 and D12.
They produced RTC, partition deed etc. To prove it.
Previously this land was standing in the name of ancestors of the defendants.
In view of the land acquisition caused by Hon'ble Supreme Court, the plaintiff cannot contend that he is in lawful possession of the property.
Apart from it, the physical possession of the property was handed over to the defendants by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
Therefore, the O.S. No. 2814/2015 plaintiff is not in possession of this property.

Further,
since the defendants are owners of land No. 67/1, It cannot be termed that putting up construction in their property does not amounts to interference in the possession of the plaintiffs.
The plaintiff failed to prove the lawful possession of suit property on the date of filing of the suit and the plaintiff has also failed to prove the alleged interference by the defendants.
Hence I answer Issue No. 1 to 3 in negative.
20. Issue No. 4: For the foregoing reasons, I pass the following ORDER.
